name: Knight Latin Peaks
rules_text: Fill the 5x5 grid with digits 1-5 so that no digit repeats in any row or column. In addition, two cells a chess knight's move apart must never hold the same digit. Clues describe three consecutive cells in a line.
clue_text: Each clue names three consecutive cells in a row or column and says that the middle one is a peak (larger than both ends), a valley (smaller than both ends), that the three are strictly increasing or decreasing in reading order, or gives their sum. Some cells are given outright.

name: Gapped Rows
rules_text: Fill the 5x5 grid with digits 1-5 so that every row contains each digit exactly once. Columns may repeat digits, but any two vertically adjacent cells must differ by at least 2. Clues give relations between adjacent cells.
clue_text: Clues are statements about adjacent cells: a horizontal pair is ordered ('<' or '>'), differs by an exact amount, or has a given sum; a vertical pair is ordered or has a given sum. Some cells are given outright.

name: Diagonal Echo
rules_text: Fill the 5x5 grid with digits 1-5 so that no digit repeats in any row, column, or in either of the two main diagonals. Clues relate cells that touch at a corner or along an edge.
clue_text: Clues compare two touching cells: equal (only possible for diagonal neighbours), ordered with '<' or '>', a given sum, or a given difference. Some cells are given outright.

name: Even Windows
rules_text: Fill the 4x4 grid with digits 1-5 so that no digit repeats in any row or column (each line therefore omits one digit). Every 2x2 window of four adjacent cells must have an even digit sum. Clues point out extremes in lines and relations between neighbours.
clue_text: Clues say that a given cell is the largest or the smallest digit in its whole row or column, or relate two adjacent cells ('<', '>' or a given sum). Some cells are given outright.
